meta_description: Chain-of-custody evidence is becoming a market-access requirement, not a marketing story.

blocks.x: Chain-of-custody evidence is becoming a market-access requirement, not a marketing story.

EUDR made provenance a compliance deadline is not a slogan; it is a delivery position. The evidence is consistent across industries — the constraint is rarely technology; it is whether the operating model takes this seriously from sprint one.

items: Capture at source (mobile-first for farmers) decides data quality more than ledger choice.
Role-based verification: regulators, buyers and auditors each see only what their role permits.
Verified provenance is premium positioning: the market pays for proof.

blocks.x: Three questions to ask your current vendors

items: Where exactly does the evidence for each claim live — and can your auditor reach it without a project?
Who signs the go/no-go gate, and what evidence do they require before signing?
What did you stop last quarter, and what did the stop save us?

blocks.x: The failure mode is predictable: enthusiasm funds the demo, budget cycles gate the industrialization, and by the time the governance conversation starts, shadow usage has already created the exposure the review was meant to prevent.

items: Pre-agreed criteria and locked baselines before build; the demo is the least important artifact.
Named owners, run models and escalation paths agreed with the operating team, not for it.
Replay trails, control tests and documentation as artifacts of the build — never reconstructed.

blocks.x: Regulator queries that took weeks of document hunts now resolve in hours with anchored evidence.
